Hi Chris — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete decision points we flagged on the call: 

1) Workload profile: you mentioned an initial pilot peaking ~350 qps (short prompts), with production target ~1.2k qps within 6 months.
2) Latency SLO: sub-200ms median for simple prompts; 95th target ~400ms.
3) Data residency & PHI: MediSyn will handle PHI and requires EU/US separation for patient records; some datasets will remain in your VPC.
4) Isolation concerns: procurement and engineering asked for clarity on noisy-neighbor risk if we run on our hosted plane vs Dedicated or Private.

My recommendation based on the above: start pilot on Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) to guarantee throughput and isolation while we validate integration. For long-term, evaluate Private VPC if PHI boundaries prove restrictive and you need full control over egress. Hosted API is lower friction but harder to give the guarantees you described.

Please see the attached deployment-eval-checklist and the short QPS/latency spreadsheet — fill any missing numbers and send back. Specific asks for you:
- Confirm whether pilot traffic will include PHI or only de-identified test data.
- Confirm expected concurrency distribution (percent of requests that hit short vs long context).
- Any contractual minimums or procurement timing we should be aware of.

Next steps I propose:
- You return the checklist by EOD Wednesday (6-Oct)
- Redwood will produce a dedicated capacity sizing and a Private/VPC migration estimate within 3 business days of receiving the checklist
- We'll set up a short tech call with our infra lead (Stephanie) to walk isolation boundaries and SLO guarantees.

Thanks — I looped Rachel (CS lead) and Stephanie (solutions lead) to coordinate pricing and architecture.

Camila / Rachel — attaching a short draft note (pasted below) and ballpark pricing. I kept it concise for procurement but can expand.

--- Draft technical note (summary) ---
1) Dedicated vs Hosted — isolation controls
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (no multi-tenant scheduling inside the pool), tenant-specific runtime instances, KV cache partitioning, and strict resource quotas at the pod level. This means noisy-neighbor risk is effectively eliminated inside the Dedicated pool; we control scheduling and can prioritize your traffic.
- Hosted: shared serving fleet with workload-aware routing and soft isolation. We use auto-burst shaping and cache partitioning but cannot guarantee hard isolation — risk remains under extreme noisy bursts.

2) SLOs we can reasonably commit to for Dedicated (pilot sizing assumption: 350 qps, production 1.2k qps):
- p50 token latency: <120ms (short prompts)
- p95 token latency: <350ms (short prompts)
- Availability (Dedicated SLA): 99.9% monthly uptime
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to a warmed compatible model variant in another pool/region; queueing/backpressure policies with 30s overall request timeout

3) Private VPC tradeoffs
- Provides customer-managed network and KMS/HSM integration, on-prem option for air-gapped requirements.
- Adds ~2-4 week onboarding for initial setup and networking; extra operational overhead for patching and upgrades.

4) Ballpark pricing (monthly) — very high level
- Pilot (350 qps reserved): $18k - $26k / month (includes reserved GPU hours, support)
- Production (1.2k qps reserved): $55k - $78k / month
- Private VPC add-on: one-time setup $25k - $40k + monthly platform fee ~$10k
